extraction.Name: Sarah Colombe formerly Sarah Prue
extraction.Refused/Protested: No. Did you ask for that patent? No.
extraction.Recorded patent: It was sent to me by mail at Okreek in 1920.
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: I first mortgaged and then sold it.
extraction.Buyer: the banker to whom I sold the land
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: I think the banker to whom I sold the land took advantage of the mortgage and told me that I would sooner or later lose the land and I might as well sell it. I got $1500 in cash and the remainder went to pay commission taxes and interest.
extraction.NOTES: Sold land for $3500.00; received $1500 in cash, remainder went to pay commission, taxes, and interest; six people depend on her including her husband; states 'I should rather the patent had not been issued'; signed receipt for patent; notarized May 7, 1929 by S. W. Cross, Notary Public, commission expires 4-28-32; document number 424 | TASK 5 BULK ALLOTMENT RECOVERY 2026-04-29: Sonnet text-extraction captured the allotment number from the source page header but classified it in NOTES as a 'document number' / 'Document No.' / 'No. NNNN' instead of placing it in the structured Allotment number field. The hypothesis that these document/file references are actually allotment numbers was confirmed via BLM cross-reference (exemplars: Eugene Means 2249, Lucy Patton 6802). This patch corrects 49 records via bulk regex extraction from NOTES with user-supervised review of every HIGH-confidence proposal.

recovery_notes.rationale: Source page header contained 'No. NNNN' which Sonnet captured in NOTES as 'document number' rather than placing in structured Allotment field. Hypothesis confirmed via BLM cross-reference.
